name: CGI Inc.
moat_justification: Moderate/narrow moat in IT services: backlog at 1.9x revenue, >100% book-to-bill, long-term managed-services contracts and government incumbency give contracted visibility and some switching friction, and company-reported ROIC has stayed above the cost of capital (16.0% FY2023/FY2024) — but it is falling (13.6% FY2025), the model is labor-based and won by competitive bidding against Accenture-scale rivals, and AI automation threatens headcount-based services economics. fundamentals.json carries no roic_proxy or gross-margin series for this IFRS filer (operating income is untagged in companyfacts), so the moat evidence uses CGI's own reported ROIC and adjusted EBIT margin (16.4% FY2025) instead. A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 25 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BUYBACK_TAILWIND: share count shrinking 2.9%/yr — already credited via the growth adjustment

FX_CONVERTED: reporting currency CAD converted to USD at period-end ECB reference rates (frankfurter.app) — flow facts use the period-end rate, not a period average; the rates used are recorded in dcf_numbers.json fx_conversion

ADS_RATIO_APPLIED: 40-F filer — per-share figures scaled x1.0 ordinary shares per ADS (CGI Inc. Form 40-F for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025 (filed 2025-12-17), cover page: 'Securities registered or to be registered pursuant to Section 12(b) of the Act: Class A subordinate voting shares — GIB — New York Stock Exchange'; outstanding at period end 195,939,991 Class A subordinate voting shares and 24,122,758 Class B shares (multiple voting)) so they are comparable to the ADS price; TTM pins are taken as per-ADS already
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier D (9.5%) vs bull-case tier B (15.0%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: Durable IT-services compounder, moat 5/10 — does not clear 15% at $75.57 on the normalized median base of $5.93/share: weighted IRR 12.4%, weighted IV@15% $59.21; clears 15% only below ~$59.21, and the base is stale (engine history ends FY2024; FY2025 is filed but not yet in EDGAR companyfacts), so size it like the bear end of its C.
moat_for: Backlog of CAD 31.79B at Q3 FY2026, 1.9x annual revenue, with trailing book-to-bill of 108.1% — multi-year contracted visibility
Long-term managed-services and outsourcing contracts plus a local relationship model create real, if rebid-limited, switching friction
Scale: 94,000 consultants, one of the largest independent IT and business consulting firms, with deep government-sector incumbency
Durable profitability through the cycle: adjusted EBIT margin held at 16.2-16.5% across FY2023-FY2025 and OE was positive 5 of the last 5 engine-history years
Company-reported ROIC stayed above the cost of capital through the cycle (16.0% FY2023/FY2024, 13.6% FY2025)
moat_against: Labor-based services model: contracts are won through competitive bidding, with price pressure and rebid risk at every renewal
No proprietary product or platform lock-in; rivals include Accenture and larger global integrators plus lower-cost offshore providers
AI automation is a structural threat to headcount-based IT services economics — CGI's own MD&A flags failure to adapt offerings to AI as a risk to revenue and cash flow
Company-reported ROIC is falling: 16.0% in FY2023 and FY2024 to 13.6% in FY2025
Growth is low-single-digit in constant currency (Q3 FY2026 revenue +1.3% cc) and client IT budgets are cyclical
Serial-acquisition model carries recurring restructuring/integration charges (FY2025 adjustments of CAD 213.2M net of tax)
